texts.orig: Abstract-This abstract describes the fundamental shift currently happening within the domain of urban surveillance systems. From a passive forensic approach consisting of analyzing visual data after an event (and therefore conducting post-event analysis) to implementing real-time intelligence solutions that allow action to be taken during an incident, urban surveillance methods today depend heavily on manually monitoring vast amounts of visual information. This is a labor-intensive process which often results in slow response times and a greater risk for human error when trying to assess the information being received.

texts.orig: To address these issues, the authors are providing and introducing a new framework called "ARGUS", a context-aware multimodal intelligence platform capable of delivering actionable insights for safe monitoring. The system combines three highly optimized and innovative components: intelligent visual detection using YOLOv8 for human and weapon identification; sound location through combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with a transformer for accurately locating screams; and an audio processing system for detecting angry voices.

texts.orig: This segment describes the ARGUS system, which is a contextual and multimodal behavioral intelligence system used for safety surveillance in urban areas. The primary concept of ARGUS is that reliable threat detection cannot be based on one sense input only but can be achieved through integration of visual and auditory sensing capabilities. This is accomplished by the integrated framework that ARGUS uses to collect sensory inputs, analyze temporal changes, and generate readable threat assessment outputs.

The architecture consists of three major subsystems (i) visual intelligence, (ii) acoustic intelligence and (iii) multimodal fusion and contextual reasoning. The subsystems work together and independently to provide robustness and scalability.
